evidence.text: Reason for referral: Evaluation of exertional chest tightness and shortness of breath over the past six weeks in a 68-year-old woman with hypertension and hyperlipidemia.

Findings: Normal sinus rhythm at 76 bpm. Normal axis. PR interval 164 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 421 ms.
Impression: Normal sinus rhythm with no acute ST-T wave changes.

LIPID PANEL
Total Cholesterol: 224 mg/dL (H)
LDL Cholesterol: 141 mg/dL (H)
HDL Cholesterol: 52 mg/dL
Triglycerides: 155 mg/dL (H)

BASIC METABOLIC PANEL
Sodium: 139 mmol/L
Potassium: 4.2 mmol/L
Chloride: 103 mmol/L
CO2: 25 mmol/L
BUN: 16 mg/dL
Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL
Glucose: 98 mg/dL
Calcium: 9.4 mg/dL

Lisinopril 20 mg by mouth once daily
Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg by mouth once daily
Atorvastatin 20 mg by mouth once daily at bedtime
Aspirin 81 mg by mouth once daily

EXAM:
General: well appearing, no distress.
Cardiac exam: regular rate and rhythm, normal S1 and S2, no murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Extremities: no peripheral edema.
